use_case: Water-quality anomaly detection: a feature of the remote monitoring service that learns normal patterns from 2 years of plant trend data and sends an alert when readings (chlorine residual, pump speed, well flows, tank levels, pressure) combine in an unusual way
vendor_or_model: Remote monitoring vendor (built-in time-series anomaly detection feature of its SaaS; not generative)
build_or_buy: Configure (vendor feature turned on and signals selected by the company)
data_categories: Process and water quality data from the plant and remote sites (Restricted OT data under POL-04); no personal information
affects_individuals: Yes (indirectly: the 2,850 people served, through operator decisions)
human_in_the_loop: Advisory only. The operator who receives an alert confirms with a grab sample, a second instrument, or a site check before any process change; public notice decisions stay with the Chief Operator and Owner; fixed alarms and the alarm dialer remain the alarms of record; no write path to the PLC
applicable_laws: 40 CFR 141.403(b)(3)(i)(A) compliance monitoring and 141.202 public notice unchanged; C-WATER-R01 readiness only (300i-2(a)(1)(A)(iii) monitoring practices; (b)(4) detection strategies) if the population served passes 3,300
status: Proposed (free trial since 2026-06-15; continued as advisory only to 2026-10-31; not approved as a monitoring control)

use_case: General-purpose public generative AI chatbots used by office staff to draft customer letters and notices
data_categories: Risk of Restricted information (SCADA details, device passwords) or customer information being pasted
human_in_the_loop: Staff write and approve every letter; public notices use the approved templates
applicable_laws: Fla. Stat. 501.171 if customer personal information were entered; company policy POL-04 4.8 and POL-02 C.2
status: Approved for Public information only (Low tier on that basis; entering Restricted or customer information is prohibited and would make it High)
